content.value_statement: Public data authorization projects combine policy, procurement, commercial, security, and deadline risks. This skill organizes those decisions into practical analyses, plans, checklists, and draft materials.
actual_capabilities: Compares whole, sector-based, and scenario-based authorization models and explains their practical fit.
Outlines the five-stage authorization process from data catalog preparation through operating oversight.
Structures application, presentation, agreement, compliance, and renewal deliverables.
Designs fixed-fee, revenue-share, minimum-guarantee, and profit-share approaches with audit considerations.
Builds schedules around three-year registration and five-year authorization periods.
Checks data scope, security responsibility, transfer restrictions, exit terms, and raw-data trading limits.
limitations: The skill does not provide binding legal, regulatory, procurement, or government approval advice.
Local rules and current notices must be verified with official sources before action.
Recommendations depend on accurate regional, organizational, financial, and data-scope information.
The skill cannot submit applications, negotiate with authorities, or operate data systems.

use_cases.title: Assess a Regional Opportunity
use_cases.description: Compare local policy readiness, available data domains, eligibility requirements, and organizational fit before committing resources.

use_cases.title: Structure an Authorization Program
use_cases.description: Prepare a program outline covering authorization mode, data scope, operator selection, oversight, security, and exit conditions.

use_cases.title: Review Commercial and Compliance Terms
use_cases.description: Examine revenue sharing, audit rights, responsibility boundaries, prohibited uses, registration renewal, and authorization expiry.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Authorization Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the three public data authorization models for [region]. Compare eligibility, competition, operating scope, and major compliance obligations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner comparison of available operating models

prompt_templates.title: Assess Organizational Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [organization] for a [sector] public data opportunity in [region]. Identify evidence gaps, stakeholders, and the next five actions.

prompt_templates.title: Outline an Authorization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an authorization plan outline for [scenario]. Cover data scope, term, security duties, prohibited uses, oversight, exit, and registration renewal.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agreement and Revenue Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed agreement and revenue model: [details]. Flag legal, security, audit, transfer, termination, registration, and five-year authorization risks.

output_examples.input: Compare sector-based and scenario-based authorization for a regional transport data service.
output_examples.output: Start with scenario-based authorization when the service and data scope are narrow. Consider sector-based authorization when capabilities, funding, and oversight can support broader operations.

output_examples.input: Review a five-year authorization with a three-year registration.
output_examples.output: The terms can overlap, but registration may expire first. Assign renewal ownership and begin renewal preparation at least three months before registration expiry.

output_examples.input: Suggest a revenue model for a new public data product with uncertain demand.
output_examples.output: Consider a modest minimum guarantee plus revenue sharing. Define revenue, deductions, reporting frequency, audit rights, late payment, and adjustment rules before launch.

best_practices: Verify every policy citation and deadline against current national and local official sources.
Define data scope, responsibility boundaries, audit evidence, prohibited uses, and exit conditions before commercial negotiation.
Maintain separate reminders for registration renewal and authorization renewal, with named owners and evidence requirements.
anti_patterns: Do not treat early stakeholder engagement as permission to bypass transparent selection or procurement rules.
Do not market, transfer, or sell raw public data without explicit lawful authority.
Do not use sample revenue ratios or timelines as guaranteed local requirements.

faq.question: What authorization models does the skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers whole, sector-based, and scenario-based authorization, including selection factors and operator implications.

faq.question: Can this skill determine whether my organization qualifies?
faq.answer: It can structure a readiness assessment. Qualification still requires verification against the current local notice and selection rules.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports issue identification and document planning, but qualified counsel and relevant authorities must confirm legal conclusions.

faq.question: Can authorized operators sell raw public data?
faq.answer: The source guidance states that raw public data should not be traded. Products require lawful processing, authorization, and compliance review.

faq.question: How does the skill handle authorization and registration dates?
faq.answer: It tracks them separately and recommends advance renewal preparation because registration may expire before authorization.

faq.question: Can it draft a complete application or agreement?
faq.answer: It can produce a structured draft from supplied facts. Users must validate local requirements, evidence, approvals, and final legal language.
